question: Can augmentation fill account for at least half the previously observed Y9-X9 development-novel loss gap?
status: posthoc_hypothesis_from_old_development_and_test; source-only new fits; no independent confirmation
only_treatment: translation fill128 versus one source-calibrated gray; original224RGB content, retained pixel positions and clipping identical
replacement_rule: round(median of original source-camera0 fourcorner gray references), labels/outcomes not used for this value
encoder_preprocess_readout_normalizer: reuse original fixed encoder, exact preprocessing, source scalar transform, CE+lambda=.01 and optimizer; no baseline/constant-arm refits
primary: I=(oldY-oldX)-(neutralY-neutralX), equal mean over10 physical development objects
implementation_explanation_screen: abs(neutralY_loss-neutralX_loss)<=0.5*old_development_novel_gap AND neutralY_loss<oldY_loss. I remains the signed interaction; report X absolute change and both angle regimes. Passing does not mean Y improvement accounts for half, nor that matched fill is better overall.
intervals: none; finite development10-object descriptive effects, not independently confirmed
source_training_convergence: gradient infinity<=1e-5 finite; do not tune if fails
causal_limit: Identifies this deterministic fill treatment within a fixed training pipeline; does not identify CNN internal mechanism, real stereo geometry, natural-world causal effect, general augmentation utility or originality.
